answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy can be pushed onto sponsors. A new key joins only when an established key vouches for it, and the sponsor's k-th vouch locks 40×k² POA: three vouches lock 560, yet a sponsor of 1,000 keys must lock roughly 13.4 billion, close to sixteen times what one epoch mints. Bonds stay frozen for a 20-epoch velvet period. A falcon audit samples 3% of sponsored keys per epoch; if one is caught passing off a recycled answer as a fresh fable, the sponsor forfeits all its vouch bonds. Weakness: farms recruiting many unrelated sponsors, each of whom carries the risk.
